john_acme: Hey team — since yesterday we're seeing a spike of 503s on bulk embeddings. Calls from our worker (sdk v1.3.2) hit 503 for ~8% of batches during a 20k-vector job. Request IDs: r-abc123, r-def456. No infra changes on our side, no increased parallelism. Any known incidents?

alex: Sorry about that — we'll triage. Can you paste a minimal repro request (headers + approximate body size) and confirm concurrency and batch size? Also one full request ID would help.

john_acme: Minimal repro info: batch_size=512, concurrency=6, vectors ~20k total. Example curl (redacted keys):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input": [ ... 512 vectors ... ] }'
```
Request id r-abc123 returned 503 with body "upstream unavailable".

samir: FYI SDK 1.3.2 has a retry aggressiveness bug that can amplify load. 1.3.4 includes a safer jittered exponential backoff and optional idempotency tokens for embeddings. Short-term: set max_concurrency=2 and enable retry backoff. Example (python sdk):
```python
client = RedwoodClient(max_concurrency=2, retry_policy={"backoff":{"type":"jitter","base_ms":200}})
```

ingrid: From infra side: seeing elevated 5xx at the ingress LB between ~15:50-17:20 UTC yesterday. Patterns show a mix of TCP resets then 503s emitted by gateway when upstream worker pools briefly exhausted. Log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T16:07:22Z edge[lb-3] upstream reset 
2026-03-15T16:07:22Z gateway worker exhausted connections=64 pool_wait_ms=312
```
We're pulling connection pool metrics now.

maria: We reproduced in staging by replaying a similar workload: multiple concurrent batch uploads with concurrency=6 and batch_size=512 consistently produced 503s after ~30s of steady load. Root cause looks like connection pool exhaustion at the proxy under long-lived uploads plus aggressive client retries. Working mitigations: lower keepalive, add early backpressure + connection limits.

alex: Short-term mitigation deployed to canary: ingress keepalive lowered to 30s; per-IP rate limit (12 r/s) added; and we've changed behavior so overload returns 429 with Retry-After instead of 503 when queue fills. Canary metrics look better (503 rate down ~90% on canary).

john_acme: Appreciate that — can you confirm whether we'll be billed for retries? We noticed our billing spike during the incident window.

alex: We will not retroactively bill for server 5xx failures in the incident window — support will issue account credits for confirmed cases. For duplicate successful requests caused by aggressive client retry loops, we'll review on a case-by-case basis. I'm opening a billing ticket and will CC you.

maria: Longer-term plan: add server-side token bucket throttling and a fast-fail path so overloaded clients get 429 early. Also plan per-route concurrency limits and queue size observability. ETA: rollout to prod next week after QA.

samir: Immediate recommendation for customers: upgrade to SDK v1.3.4 (includes retry safety for embeddings), reduce max_concurrency to 2 for large-batch jobs, and add idempotency tokens for large batches. Example: 
```python
# pseudo
client = RedwoodClient(version=\"1.3.4\", max_concurrency=2)
client.embeddings.create(input=batch, idempotency_key=str(uuid4()))
```

support-bot: incident-created:INC-2026-0315-embeds-spike assigned to eng-infra.

john_acme: Testing now with v1.3.4 + concurrency=2. Will report back in ~30m.

alex: Thanks — can you DM one failing request body (r-abc123) so we can attach it to the infra ticket? Also we'll track billing ticket. :thumbsup:

john_acme: PM'ed r-abc123 payload and logs. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.

alex: Closing this thread for now — canary appears healthy. We'll post a follow-up when the full rollout completes across regions. If you still see 503s, please reopen.
